claim: Removing the write from the read path (_stamp CTE) eliminates lock-based stalls of recall under concurrent writes: paired isolated benches (fresh 0.17.0 vs fresh 0.18.0, identical 9,326-lesson / 74,778-edge corpus, identical query set, n=40 each) show under-write-load median 23.4 ms -> 15.4 ms (1.5x) and p95 372 ms -> 178 ms (2.1x), with worst-case bounded instead of lock-convoy stalls up to statement_timeout observed in production. Quiet-system median is UNCHANGED within noise (9.7 ms -> 10.9 ms).
criterion: under-load p95 improves >= 1.5x AND quiet median does not regress by more than 20%

methodology.environment: dedicated pgvector/pgvector:pg17 container, no other load; corpus copied from production; ANALYZE run; 3 warmup queries
methodology.load: 3 writer threads, each looping UPDATE of 20 random lessons

corrections.why_withdrawn: The 44.2 ms 'before' was measured on the live cluster where concurrent fleet writes made the recency stamp block on locks; the paired isolated re-measurement shows the quiet-system medians are equal and the entire benefit is contention behavior, not intrinsic per-call cost. Earlier gate runs are preserved below as history with their original hybrid-install caveat.
corrections.history_hybrid_state_note: Earlier after-side runs (3.2-4.3 ms median, 3,609-lesson corpus) were taken with 0.18.0 function bodies applied via psycopg2 onto a 0.17.0 extension catalog; pgmnemo_version was honestly stamped '0.17.0+perf-patch' and correctly rejected by the release pre-flight.
